plumbingTest_exactInverseCurve_vs_SDR_or.note: Synthetic HDR made from an SDR original by linear scaling; tonemap=none is its exact inverse, so a correct pipeline must reproduce the original. The production curve (hable) is deliberately NOT an inverse, so scoring it against that original is meaningless (it scored VMAF ~11 and darker) — an earlier draft of this test wrongly used it and was discarded.

realHdr10Visual: hdr-brightdoor-naive-washed-out.jpg vs hdr-brightdoor-tonemapped.jpg: same frame; the naive conversion is grey and flat, the tone-mapped frame has proper contrast, deep blacks and natural warm colour.
timeModelFinding: Predicted vs actual encode seconds: 20 vs 39.6, 20 vs 27.4, 33 vs 22, 46 vs 31. High-bitrate 10-bit HEVC ran up to 1.98x slower than predicted, so HDR estimates are scaled x2 (TONEMAP_SAFETY_FACTOR).
limits: No real iPhone file was available; iPhone-style inputs are synthetic and real HDR10 is PQ, not iPhone HLG/Dolby Vision.
Tone-mapping curve is hable with npl=100 (FFmpeg-documented chain); it is a look choice, not a colour-accurate reference, and was judged by eye plus the plumbing test.
Dolby Vision RPU metadata is ignored (the HLG/HDR10 base layer is used).
